source_refs.note: Exercise 14.4 Q2, book p.289 (PDF 294). No answer in the key (verification); all three products = 117 (sympy). Solution book PDF 1269-1270 agrees.

blocks.explanation:
A verification question about the cyclic property of the scalar triple product.
We must compute all three products and see that they are equal.
Plan: find each cross product first (the cross is always done before the dot), then dot it with the remaining vector.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = 3\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = 4\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{c} = 2\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
To verify: \(\underline{a} \cdot (\underline{b} \times \underline{c}) = \underline{b} \cdot (\underline{c} \times \underline{a}) = \underline{c} \cdot (\underline{a} \times \underline{b})\).
Method: \(\underline{a} \cdot \underline{b} \times \underline{c}\) means \(\underline{a} \cdot (\underline{b} \times \underline{c})\): a dot of a vector with a scalar has no meaning. Use the determinant formula for each cross product.

Compare and check
\[117 = 117 = 117 \;\checkmark\]
\[\begin{vmatrix} 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 4 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 117\]
Why: All three are equal, as the cyclic property says. The single determinant \([\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}]\) gives the same 117, a further check.
